title: Extremal trees for the biharmonic index
scope: For every n >= 5, every finite vertex type V with card V = n and every tree G on V: bh(star on n vertices) <= bh G <= bh(path on n vertices), with equality on the left iff G is isomorphic to the star and on the right iff G is isomorphic to the path, where bh G = (card V) times the sum over nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues of lambda^(-2).
validation: Seventeen modules compiled and kernel-checked from an empty build by an independent reviewer, who read every module; a transitive closure of 36,296 constants has only the three permitted axioms and no unsafe or partial constant; Lean controls from the literal eigenvalues give BH(K2)=1/2, BH(K_{1,4})=76/5, BH(fork)=124/5 and BH(P5)=38 and distinguish the no-factor-n, power-1 and no-multiplicity models; statement fidelity PASS against the source and the literal. Root verified receipts, hashes and the mathlib pin, and read and hand-checked the paper.
substantive_reason: Settles in full a deliberate conjecture stated in a peer-reviewed paper and retained verbatim in its journal final, which concretizes Problem 6.3 of Wei, Li and Yang, still open in their v2. The source proves no upper bound for general trees. No complete bridge from any read theorem exists: coefficient monotonicity fails because BH = W^2/n - 2 c_3 is a difference of two terms that both rise toward the path, and majorization, Newton-type inequalities and Lyapunov interpolation do not close it. It is not a spectral parameter instance on the path side, since the argument breaks at k = 3.
contrary_scope_assessment: This is close to the line and significance is recorded as modest. The proof is about one page, close in method to the classical Wiener-index argument one moment higher, and introduces no new invariant. The star half is easy, and a second reviewer gives a one-paragraph law for it, unreviewed. Both adversarial reviewers recommended credit at low or low-to-moderate confidence; the second said a root exclusion on significance would be defensible. Root accepted because the campaign rule says a template analogy without a complete reduction is not an exclusion. The user may overrule.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded source-primary investigation, not worldwide priority certification.
prior_limits: No citation index. Zhou LAA 429 (2008), Liu-Liu AML 24 (2011), Das-Xu-Liu LAA 439 (2013) and Chen-Das DM 338 (2015) are unread; Wei-Li-Yang cite them and leave the tree problem open. MATCH 91(2) 285-286 is closed, unread and unidentified; if it bears on this conjecture the acceptance must be revisited. Gutman 2004, A New Hyper-Wiener Index, was read in abstract only and its full text is closed after HTTP 418. Modified hyper-Wiener indices in the literature are the Laplacian coefficient c_{n-3}, not the squared family, and no printed extremal theorem for the squared family was found. Registry roots closed.
process_adjudication: Disclosed and judged non-substantive: some displays in the review and qualification lanes ran over the 15000-character limit; two failed scope-reading runs in the second qualification were repaired with new labelled runs; sealing reruns in the Lean lane and the second qualification; a scratch groff test failed in the manuscript lane. Certificate content rests on the fresh replay and independent audit rather than on those histories.
trust_limits: Upstream Lean, mathlib and their oleans are trusted through pins and were not rebuilt. Reviewers are AI systems, not human referees, and the reviewers and the final Lean author share a model family. Only the spectral form of BH is formalized; the source also prints the double-distance form as equal.
paper_corrections: Root removed status lines and internal paths, repaired one Lean quotation, corrected one description of the source (Theorem 5.5 gives exact values or bounds), made small precision edits and fixed page layout; see qa/ROOT-CORRECTIONS.json. The proof structure and algebra were not changed.
not_claimed: Any statement about the sum of lambda^(-k) for k other than 2
The unreviewed star-side law as a separate result
